newsitem.title: USA: Jewish jaywalker vindicated in U.S. court case.
newsitem.headline: Jewish jaywalker vindicated in U.S. court case.

text.p: An orthodox Jewish man charged with jaywalking and forced to sit in a police car against his religious principles agreed to accept $7,000 in damages from the city of Cincinnati, his attorney said on Tuesday.

David Becker, 27, now of Los Angeles, agreed to the settlement on Monday just before his civil lawsuit against the city was to begin in Hamilton County Common Pleas Court, his attorney Kenneth Lawson said.
Cincinnati policewoman Monica Gaynor arrested Becker in September 1994 for allegedly walking against a traffic light while on his way home from attending temple services.

She forced him to sit in her police cruiser and sign the jaywalking citation even though it is against his religion to get into a car and carry a wallet with identification on the Jewish sabbath. The officer told Becker he would be jailed if he did not comply.
The jaywalking charge was later dismissed.
The case prompted the city's police department to modify its training to incorporate sensitivity to religious practices.
